I’ve been using this app for over 3 years, I love it. It works just fine on Mac. Recently, I got a PC and I moved my workspace there. There is a webpage version of this app but it doesn’t sync right. I was writing on my PC yesterday for all night and I woke up today check the same file on my phone. BOOM, nothing is there, nothing got saved. And the worst part is, the website will auto sync to the phone no matter what. Which means it will erase whatever I wrote on the website and go back to the old version of the file on my phone. ISN’T THIS STUPID?

这个软件真的哪里都好，就是这个在windows上跟mac的sync会出问题。不会即时同步，总是会以mac的版本为准。导致在windows上写的东西存不下来，一刷新就消失。又因为这个丢了一次东西，web到底怎么回事。

This app has so many features that allow you to organize info under appropriate headers, and sub-headers! Once you get the hang of it you’ll have a cleanly organized listing of your data. 
> You will likely find yourself resetting the hierarchy of data in order to keep it organized in the area(s) where it belongs — otherwise you’ll find data under the correct Headers but in several locations. 
🔅With patience & time you can organize it into a clean collection of your data.

I’m a big notes guy, and used to always just use the Notes app from Apple, but one day I needed to just scribble a drawing to get my point across and couldn’t do it, found this app and the rest is history. Everything from the super clean interface, to the quick and efficient way to jot down notes and label them with hashtags to help  categorize things - it’s seamless and honestly, one of the quickest subscriptions ive ever paid for. I use it daily, if not hourly
i feel like all the other note taking apps are more for aesthetic but i like that this one is actually practical and everything isn’t locked behind a paywall
Love Bear, love everything about it. And the recent addition of mermaid and workspace as tags just keep making it better. It truly is a dream app.

I love this app!! I love the different themes available, I love the live updates for the time of an entry, & I love the pin to top feature. I use this app for notes, to save links & package tracking numbers. I would like to suggest each entry show the day of the week, & the time. I also would like to suggest entries be stored together by each different month. Thank you for this app!! I use this app every day.

title.label: I’ve never written a review but this deserved one

content.label: I’ve used every note app in the App Store and always end up back on my iPhone notes app…until now. It’s perfect. Visually refined. Clean. The typography is so refreshing. I believe it’s their font which is cool. Shows they care. One of the reasons the other apps frustrate me is they’re all too clunky. This one is as simple as Notes but has every possible features cleverly hidden. The way menus are built is so intuitive. Endless ways to easily organize without the clutter of endless folders. You can customize everything. I can’t believe I’m saying this but it makes me feel good using it. lol Incredible job by the developers. Please make other apps. This level of artistry in app design is desperately needed. The craziest part it’s $30 a YEAR! Immediately cancelled my Evernote subscription which was $12 a month and sucks compared to this app.

I love this app. I have been using it for probably several years at this point. I have kept everything in my notes, and I happen to tap too fast getting into the app, thinking I’m getting a “leave a review” pop up; they asked to make storage on my device and EVERYTHING is deleted, not even in the trash can, I mean completely gone! I hope there is a way to get them back, I hadn’t made any backups 🥲

title.label: Good markdown viewer, not a fan of tags, expensive subscription

content.label: I’m looking for a new Notes app. I like the color themes that Bear offers. The app looks really good too. The text and paragraph formatting options are limited though. Bear is good as a markdown viewer. What I don’t like, however: 1) in order to create folders and nested folders, I have to use tags 2) I was also very turned off by the subscription.. $30 a year? I’d like to see a  reasonable one-time pay, or reasonable yearly subscription price. $30 a year is patently absurd if you’re not a heavy user and only just using the app as a markdown viewer.

Sure it looks "clean" at first but it automatically adds markups that show every time you try to edit a word. So if you delete part of it you end up with bunch of asterisks to delete. That's not clean. Would prefer no markups at all. And having to pull up a secondary keyboard for every formatting task gets tiresome and kills work flow. Why not a long press menu for frequent formatting functions? And can't select more than one cell in tables. Honestly would rather go back to apple notes if wasn't so slow on my older device.

title.label: Great app at a great price

content.label: I love the Bear app. It’s WAY better than Evernote and reasonably priced. Keep up the great work!
I love this notes app is just what I needed! Though I’m giving this 4 stars because I really wish the lock notes feature would be free.

I was really excited to try this app especially since so many people love it and because I’m looking for something that is simple that also supports wiki linking. unfortunately, as a VoiceOver user, I’m finding the app very difficult to use. Many of the buttons are not labeled and also voiceover has trouble tracking focus as I move around the app. As such, the app is currently not usable for me at least on iOS. I hope that the developers will consider adding more robust voiceover support in the future, I would definitely be a very happy user..

I was looking for an Evernote alternative where I could use tags, and this is perfect. I both like to write and store recipes using tags for season, type, occasion etc. The support for nested tags is much appreciated, and their Pro plan is very reasonable. Not much is paywalled (it’s just cloud features, themes, and search), so give it a try!

It’s almost perfect, it won’t render math or PDFs or anything, it was working, the update broke it

I love how it looks but the exporting and rendering are pretty fundamental and I feel like it should really be able to do more, like why not also have rich text as an option and if it’s only markdown then it’s a pretty high priority that it should do markdown literally flawlessly and it doesn’t 

Hope it gets fixed asap 
If still recommend it but with warnings and if there were anything else better this app could easily lose to that 

There are so few options for anything like this it’s pretty mind blowing

No matter how many times I try other note taking apps, none of them come close to the simple, great experience of Bear.

Bear slaps. I've used it for like 8 years now. Super simple, just the right amount of complexity. Themes and styles are beautiful, including all the custom icons. Sync is always super fast and smooth. Exporting, tagging, formatting, all just work exactly how you'd want. title.label: ipad rendering bugged for months now

content.label: when using bear on the ipad in windowed mode (not full screen), sometimes following a link within a note causes a bug with rendering where the bottom portion of the note is not rendered. you can sometimes fix it by restarting bear.

This app is reliable, easy to navigate, and stylish. I love using it every day! Please consider adding a feature for user-made themes in the future! And a feature to toggle a note’s history + restore versions!

Hands down my favorite notes app I’ve ever used. It’s getting more features all the time and has everything I need. Most aesthetically pleasing app, too.

I love how it syncs across my iPad and MacBook, and the way it centers the content inside the window is an amazing but simple feature that not all other notes apps have.

Well worth the money. My go-to for many years now. Small development team I believe, too, so I’m more than happy supporting this gem.

Well, it was a great app, but the latest update just screwed up the copy and paste function.  Used to be you could just copy and paste, then edit your data; now after you copy, it gives you a multiple choice for paste for which no selected options work, so they just rendered my favorite note taking app useless for copying data to edit.
Love it. It’s a little glitchy sometimes but overall I love the design and feel

title.label: Almost Perfect Out of the Box

content.label:
I would give it 5 stars if there was the ability to disable word wrap in code blocks and allow a sideways scroll. I do a lot of code snippets, but most lines are beyond the iPhone Pro Max screen width. Callouts could benefit from this as well.

It would also be great if we could add or edit a CSS stylesheet file for the HTML export, or dare I ask for in-app style customizations beyond the prebuilt theme and the font face and size/spacing options (which are great by the way, thank you!)

Finally, but not an issue of this app at all and not affecting its rating, would the developers PLEASE, PRETTY PLEASE make a Windows app, or at least a web app I could use on Windows? Then I would be a diehard forever customer.

title.label: Thank you for the safe space

content.label: This app feels safe, calm, useful, simple.

title.label: I want to love it so badly

content.label:
Bear would be my perfect notes app, and I would gladly pay the subscription for it. 

However, the keyboard toolbar/text editor on iPhone is so bad, especially when compared with the default Apple notes. (Please just copy how Apple notes sets up their keyboard toolbar, it’s so much better).

If you want to format anything, it is such a headache and so incredibly slow because everything is hidden behind a formatting menu icon, which you have to press, select the formatting option you want, then change back to keyboard. This could very easily just be one button press like it is in Apple Notes. And considering how often I format notes, this time adds up quickly. Aesthetic at the cost of efficiency is useless. 

Also pls pls pls just copy the way Apple’s todo lists work. I want to be able to drag around todo list items. 

Unfortunately, Bear is an app clearly designed to be used with a mouse and keyboard, not fingers and touchscreens. I think it is so beautiful, and I love the organizational structure with the tags and markdown. But this basic functionality that is missing is so core to a notes app that I will very sadly have to replace it with Apple notes. 

If they fix this, I’m buying the subscription and changing my review to 5 stars.
It’s like it was made for me
They updated the app and absolutely everything that I’ve kept there is gone and customer service has helped very very little. If ur gonna use the app at least keep your work backed up elsewhere

I do a ton of notetaking, and Bear is now my indispensable tool for doing so. The UX is great across iPhone, iPad, and Mac, syncing across devices just works with iCloud without any extra subscription, and the Markdown support is great for portability between systems like blogs.

So easy to use and intuitive. 

The aesthetics make it fun. I haven’t found a better app for organizing all the notes, documents, links, and courses I collect and refer to to support my career-change coaching practice. 

The tagging system allows me to classify something by topic and also author or source. It’s a beautiful personal library. 

And the customer service is extremely responsive.

This app shines in the little details: it’s crazy fast, compare it to Apple notes and you will see a night and day difference, especially for long notes. It has table of contents, which makes it easy to navigate long notes. The tag system is miles better than folders. You can manage your todos by following a thin line under each of your notes that shows the progress of your todos in the note. It supports latex! So you can write math formulas now. It has web access. It has a nice menu of themes. It shows you unmentioned backlinks: you can reference other notes that mention the title of your current note. You can lock notes with attachments. You can copy links to each note. You can export to multiple formats. You can draw (although here it’s a bit basic) and have Bear detect words in your images. It gives you useful stats about your notes. And I could keep going.

You would not tell half of these when you first open the app, and that’s the point. Its power is modest. It enables you and gets out of the way so you can work. Their dev team is small and slow, but they deliver. Late sometimes, but they deliver. This app is a powerhouse.

title.label: Tried them all-came home to Bear

content.label:
This app is so streamlined that it can be deceptive how brilliant it is. Bear works with your mind—without friction. 

Hashtags are one of five key power tools here. Use them to create a filing system, as well as to cross index any files you want.

Bear seems simple, but it is in fact the most elegant writing tool out there. In its elegant simplicity exists ultimate creative power.

As a fiction writer, with many large projects on my plate, I can tell you—as someone who has tried all the excellent writing apps out there—nothing comes close to Bear.

It’s exactly what it needs to be, leaves everything else in its wake, is created by people who design with pure intent, which is why it’s literally pristine.

Even if you doubt, master its incredibly simple tools, and build out a file system using the tags— they nest like breadcrumb trails…and there you go. You no longer have to choose a folder, or even a title. Just write, just flow, just go.

I’ve had this for years and love it. Just open and start writing, and the company does NOT extract or use any of your information, location, contacts, etc., which is a great sign of integrity, especially today.
if you could send notes to people like in evernote i would drop other note apps and go full bear. upgrade it and grab the money on the table bear

I didn't even get to read  the welcome notes before deleting this app. The side menu will not stop popping out, no matter what I do. The advice was to swipe right from the middle of the screen to avoid this but nothing worked. And if the welcome notes have titles, VO didn't read them. Just skip this one. Save yourself the headache.

I’ve tried pretty much every web clipping app out there in pursuit of the perfect system to store and organize my research. Bear comes pretty close! The UI is simple and uncluttered (super important to me as someone with difficulties navigating busy designs). The nesting note system keeps all my notes and clippings well organized and easily searchable. Unlike other Markdown-based apps I tried, there was no learning curve—use was completely intuitive, so I could get to work right away. I particularly like the note menu design with its ability to assign an icon to each category—again, as someone who has difficulty navigating dense text designs, the icons provide a helpful identifier to help me quickly navigate to my most-used categories.

I’ve used Bear for a few years now. I really enjoy the functionality, UI, and ease of formatting. I have the yearly subscription, so my notes sync across devices readily. I can also adjust font, spacing, and color themes easily. I’m not an advanced Markdown user, but I’m beginning to learn more features I’ve barely touched, like making your notes into your own pseudo-wiki (!). It’s really nice.

I’ve been using Bear Notes almost from the beginning. It was slow going at first and I hung in there as Bear moved closer and closer to 2.0 and I have to tell you after using nearly all of the options that are out there for note taking, journaling and more, there’s no better.  So if you’re stuck with another note app, and want to see what else is out there, give Bear a try. You will not regret it. Excellent work developers, I look forward to being with you for years to come.

Beautiful, efficient, and versatile! This is a one-of-a-kind app that I’ve made an inextricable part of my daily flow. Truly, it’s a masterpiece of elegance in software design. My only hope is the devs keep focus, as its versatility is going to encourage adamant recommendations for all kinds of added functionality and integration that could easily pull the app in a thousand different directions. I include myself among the masses. I wish the devs would add integration with the native iOS apps, especially the calendar and reminders.
Me gusta mucho,tiene muchas opciones de texto,puedes hacer de todo un poco,es buena para ipad y teléfonos,simplemente me encanta
非常垃圾。辛苦写了几个小时的字全没了。不建议使用。
My only go to app for writing. I love it.

I’ve been using Bear for years, long before Bear 2 released and it truly has come a long way! As a student, I don’t use Bear for anything particularly professional. I’m just a person who enjoys keeping everything simple and organized. Bear is just that. It’s easy to use yet has always been steps ahead of the iOS Notes app as far as features and UI go. I use other apps for structure and organization like Obsidian, but everything I do starts in Bear. If I need to write anything at all, I open Bear without feeling overwhelmed by assigning it a category immediately. 
I’m a Bear Pro user and I don’t plan on letting go of Bear anytime soon so
here are a few tiny things I’d love to see in the future: 
1. There are a few instances where I like to be able to have a note throughout all of a tag’s subtags and main page out of convenience. For example, if I have a note called “resources” with the tags #physics/GR and #physics, currently the tag will only appear in the GR subtag. 
2. I wish the pencil icon next to external links could be disabled. 
3. It would be nice if users could adjust the primary action that appears in the menu. For example, the current first attachment action is Take Photo and any other requires you to hold down the button. I personally use the Add Images option way more so it would be more convenient if users could decide what shortcut appears on top.

Bear is one of my favorite note-taking apps. It’s beautifully designed and incredibly intuitive to use. I just wish it had an archive option — sometimes I want to hide older notes without deleting them or cluttering my daily tags. Also, the Trash folder is always visible at the top of my tags, which can be a bit distracting. It would be nicer if it were hidden or moved to the bottom. Overall, it’s an amazing app with just a couple of small things that could make it perfect.
I’ve tried multiple brand name note taking apps and this is by far my favorite. Sleek, simple and has all the features I need.

title.label: App not syncing across devices - iOS 26 broke it

content.label: App not syncing across devices - seems to have broken with iOS 26. :(

Agree with most comments.  Great UI, subpar UX.  Need to consolidate between apps and shifted to Obsidian but that’s for a personal decision across platforms and also for higher expressions of note taking that Bear doesn’t have.  One key plus is pasting  images into the note, much easier than with Obsidian. But Bear has been a great mobile app.

I replaced evernote with bear about 9 months ago and wish I had done it 2 years ago. Bear is super functional, I get pretty much everything I need. Get bear pro, it is completely worth it and the best deal of all the notes apps.

There’s been a UI revision in the last while that’s made it super confusing to do things like add images to notes from my phone (go to BIU, open a keyboard, hold down on a camera icon, etc). It’s not at all fluid.

I downloaded Bear back in 2016 and it’s been my exclusive writing app since. The interface is intuitive yet non-intrusive, something very important to me. I can write without a bunch of buttons scattered across the screen and can pull them up easily when I do need them. The tag system is amazing and easy to work with and I love the small touches like changing tag icons! I write every day and it’s thanks to Bear!
